provider: Macaulay Library / eBird (Cornell Lab of Ornithology)

free_tier.stated: No published per-account byte quota — tens of millions of assets, and Cornell explicitly positions it as backup: 'the archive serves as your personal cloud storage and backup of your media files.' Capacity is bounded by per-file and per-checklist caps, not by an account quota.

egress.terms: originals are downloadable BY THE OWNER ONLY ('your original uploaded files are available for you to download at any time by clicking the Download original link'). Public read is view/embed only; bulk research access is a manual request queue.

interface_detail: eBird checklist upload (web + Manage Media page); Macaulay Library catalog pages; no documented public write API
tooling: no CLI. The uploader is a browser tool. Media search has an API but it sits behind an Anubis proof-of-work wall.
chaining: Not chainable programmatically — the write path is a UI and the read path returns re-encoded previews, not originals, to anyone but the owner.
limits_note: photo 20 MB/file (JPG); audio 500 MB/file (WAV); video 1 GB/file (MP4/MOV/M4V, ≥720p); 20 photos + 10 audio per species per checklist; 10 video files per species

identity_cost.detail: email — eBird account is a Cornell Lab account with an email address; no institutional requirement documented.

reliability_note: Classic rule-2 pattern: upload-open, read-gated. Your own originals come back, but nobody else's do, and the media endpoints are behind Anubis PoW (search.macaulaylibrary.org/api/v1/search returned the 'Making sure you're not a bot!' interstitial).
